glossary: carolling
on Christmas Eve young people go from house to house singing carols (kolyadki) and are given sausage, bread or a coin for their sacks.
kutya
the meatless dish of boiled wheat, honey and poppy seed eaten on Christmas Eve.
varenukha
a hot drink of vodka boiled with spices, fruit and honey.
vareniki
dumplings, here with sour cream; a meat or dairy dish was forbidden on a fast day.
the Headman
the elected head of a Cossack village.
the deacon
here a church clerk who reads and sings in the choir; he is not a priest.
the Sorochintsy assessor
a district police official, feared by the villagers.
plakhta
a Ukrainian woman's wrapped skirt, worn with an apron (zapaska).
kuntush
an old-fashioned long coat of the Cossack gentry.
the Zaporozhians
free Cossacks of the lower Dnieper; their camp was called the Sich. The Empress broke up their Host in 1775.
Potemkin
Prince Grigory Potemkin, Catherine the Great's chief minister.
the man with pearl buttons
the playwright Denis Fonvizin, author of the comedy The Brigadier.
summary: On the last night before Christmas a devil steals the moon, a witch rides a broom, and the blacksmith Vakula, mocked by the proud Oksana, goes to the Empress in Petersburg for her own shoes. Gogol's funniest, warmest Christmas story.
site_description: On the last night before Christmas in the Ukrainian village of Dikanka, a devil steals the moon to get back at the blacksmith Vakula, who has painted him in hell on the church wall. The vain beauty Oksana will marry Vakula only if he brings her the shoes of the Empress. A full-cast audiobook of Nikolai Gogol's 1832 comic fairy tale, with Cossacks, witches, sacks full of lovers, and a flight to Petersburg.

ru.description: В последнюю ночь перед Рождеством чёрт крадёт месяц, чтобы отомстить кузнецу Вакуле, а гордая красавица Оксана согласна выйти за него, только если он достанет черевики самой царицы. Весёлая и добрая рождественская повесть Гоголя из «Вечеров на хуторе близ Диканьки».
